page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The server includes 1843 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the D48ds_v5 in the average performance tier for most compute and memory operations. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1630.0 and a multi-core score of 15064.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 48717.7. Stronger performance is observed in specific areas, such as image processing (14001.0 in Geekbench) and CPU encryption (43321.1 in Passmark), both ranking in the top 25%. Memory performance is also robust, with a Passmark memory score of 2757.12 and cached read-only small block bandwidth reaching 2502.0 GB/sec.

While the instance handles smaller-scale machine learning tasks adequately, generating 275.95 tokens per second for a 135M parameter LLM model, it exhibits a clear performance bottleneck on larger models. For a 70B parameter LLM, text generation drops to a weak 2.74 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. Given its balanced CPU-to-memory ratio, large local storage, and solid database operation benchmarks, this server is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, web serving, and database management.
